diagram:
flowchart TD
  TRIG["⏰ pg_cron · Mondays 12:30 UTC\nweekly, deterministic — no LLM"] --> IND["🌐 8 US FRED series\nDGS2·DGS10·UNRATE·PAYEMS·GDPC1\nCPIAUCSL·RSAFS·FEDFUNDS·DGORDER"]
  IND --> GUARD{"≥3 indicators?"}
  GUARD -->|"No"| UNKNOWN["❓ regime='unknown'\nno verdict — refuses to guess"]
  GUARD -->|"Yes"| CLASS["🧭 Weighted danger_score 0-100\ngreen<20 · yellow 20-39 · orange 40-59 · red ≥60"]
  CLASS --> WRITE["💾 macro_regime (regime+summary)\n+ macro_signals (per-indicator)"]
  UNKNOWN --> WRITE
  WRITE --> SCORES["➡️ macro_score = 100 − danger_score\nGENOME DIMENSION → weighted score → paper buys"]
  WRITE --> DISPLAY["👁️ Markets · Dashboard banner · Intelligence"]
  SCORES -.->|"US only — macro_regime has no market column"| USONLY["🇺🇸 India macro is UNAVAILABLE by construction"]
  CLASS -.->|"never"| POLICY["🚫 Does NOT change risk limits or execution"]

TRIG.label: Weekly · Mondays
TRIG.description: Supabase pg_cron job 'kairos-macro-sentinel', schedule 30 12 * * 1 — Mondays 08:30 ET. WEEKLY, not daily. Contains no LLM at all: the route imports no callLLM and no getConfiguredModel, and every number is computed deterministically. The agent_config row still naming deepseek-chat is a dead seed row from migration 031 that nothing reads.
TRIG.addReason: Every session needs a current regime read.
TRIG.changeReason: Both claims false: it is weekly (Mondays), not 'the daily pipeline', and it uses no LLM — the deepseek-chat claim came from a dead agent_config seed row.

IND.label: 8 US FRED series
IND.description: Reads FRED (not Alpha Vantage): DGS2 + DGS10 → Yield Curve 10Y-2Y, UNRATE → Sahm Rule proxy, PAYEMS → Nonfarm Payrolls, GDPC1 → Real GDP growth, CPIAUCSL → CPI inflation, RSAFS → Retail Sales, FEDFUNDS → Fed Funds Rate, DGORDER → Durable Goods. There is NO dollar series and NO volatility series. In practice only 7 of 8 ever load: CPI has never once been recorded in prod — every run since the FRED cutover is missing it.
IND.addReason: Regime is inferred from real macro data, not vibes.
IND.changeReason: Named the wrong provider (Alpha Vantage, actually FRED) and listed two series that do not exist (dollar, volatility) while omitting all 8 that do. Also records the standing 7/8 CPI gap.

GUARD.label: ≥3 indicator guard
GUARD.description: If fewer than 3 indicators load, the compute returns danger_score=null, regime='unknown', and refuses to publish a verdict. This exists because the failure it replaced was silent and confident: a zero-indicator run used to persist regime='green', danger_score=0 — indistinguishable from a genuinely calm read. Caveat: the null never reaches the table (the column is NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 and the insert coerces null→0), so downstream consumers must and do gate on the regime STRING 'unknown', never on a null score.
GUARD.addReason: The guard is the whole reason this agent can be trusted on a bad-data day, and it was invisible on the diagram.

UNKNOWN.label: regime = unknown
UNKNOWN.description: The honest no-verdict state. Consumers treat it as 'no macro evidence' rather than as a neutral reading: the research scorer marks macro unavailable and renormalizes its remaining dimensions instead of scoring a fabricated 50.
UNKNOWN.addReason: Drawn as a real terminal state so the diagram cannot imply a regime is always produced.

CLASS.label: Classify regime
CLASS.description: Computes a weighted danger_score 0-100 and maps it to a four-colour regime: green <20, yellow 20-39, orange 40-59, red ≥60. Plus an escalation override — two weight-3 indicators reading red/orange promotes yellow→orange. The enum is green/yellow/orange/red, NOT risk-on/neutral/risk-off; that three-state vocabulary belongs to a different module (the allocator), which normalizes these colours down to three.
CLASS.addReason: One label the other agents can condition on.
CLASS.changeReason: The regime enum was wrong: risk-on/neutral/risk-off is the allocator's normalized vocabulary, not this agent's output. Real bands and the escalation override added.

WRITE.label: Write macro_regime + macro_signals
WRITE.description: TWO tables, and the regime does not live in the one the old diagram named. macro_regime (upsert on week_of) holds week_of, danger_score, regime, signals_triggered, ai_bubble_score, summary, raw_indicators. macro_signals (upsert on week_of,indicator) holds only the per-indicator breakdown: indicator, value, signal, description. Neither table has a market column.
WRITE.changeReason: Claimed the regime + summary are persisted to macro_signals. They are persisted to macro_regime; macro_signals has no regime or danger_score column at all.

SCORES.label: Genome dimension
SCORES.description: danger_score is inverted into macro_score = 100 − danger_score and consumed as one of the five weighted scoring dimensions: macro_score → weighted analyst_score → direction gate → paper buys. It fails closed on staleness (>10 days) and on the <3-indicator unknown regime. This is a real path to money, not a readout.
SCORES.addReason: The single most consequential consumer was hidden inside a generic 'advisory input' arrow. 'Advisory' and 'on the money path' are not mutually exclusive and the diagram must show both.

DISPLAY.label: Display consumers
DISPLAY.description: Read-only surfaces: the Markets page gauge, the Dashboard banner when the regime is not green, and the Intelligence page. A second live consumer exists — the allocator tilts sleeve weights by regime — but it ships behind an allocation_enabled flag that is currently OFF.
DISPLAY.addReason: Splits the verified display reads from the genome path, which the old single FEED arrow conflated.

USONLY.label: US-only by construction
USONLY.description: All 8 series are US FRED series and macro_regime has no market column, so there is no India macro read and no way to store one. India names are scored with macro explicitly UNAVAILABLE and their remaining dimension weights renormalized — the system abstains rather than reusing the US regime for India.
USONLY.addReason: The US-only boundary is the reason India scoring renormalizes, and nothing on this page said so.

POLICY.label: Advisory only
POLICY.description: Verified still true in the literal sense: nothing here auto-throttles agents, changes risk limits, or halts trading — those stay deterministic and human-governed (locked decision). Read alongside SCORES: 'does not move the safety controls' is true; 'has no influence on what gets bought' is not.
POLICY.addReason: Probabilistic macro reads must not silently move safety controls.
POLICY.changeReason: Claim verified accurate and kept. Qualified only so that 'advisory' is not read as 'inert' now that macro_score is a weighted genome dimension.

history.label: Provider is FRED, not Alpha Vantage; no dollar/vol series exist; CPI has never loaded
history.reason: The node claimed it 'pulls rates, yield-curve shape, dollar, and volatility signals from Alpha Vantage'. Wrong provider and wrong series. Real source is FRED via lib/data/fred-macro.ts, and the 8 series are DGS2/DGS10 (yield curve), UNRATE (Sahm), PAYEMS, GDPC1, CPIAUCSL, RSAFS, FEDFUNDS, DGORDER. There is no dollar series and no volatility series in the code — the diagram invented two inputs and omitted all eight real ones. Verified against PROD, not just code: macro_signals shows the latest run (week_of 2026-07-13) carrying 7 indicators, and CPI Inflation has NEVER been recorded in any run, all-time. So '8 indicators' is the design and 7/8 is the lived reality; the node now says both. The CPI gap is structural rather than transient — the fetch requires exactly 13 observations and any single '.' value dropped by the finite-filter leaves 12 and fails inside a bare catch — but that is a CODE bug and is reported, not fixed here.

history.label: Weekly Mondays, not 'the daily pipeline'; and there is no LLM in this agent
history.reason: Two independent falsehoods. (1) Schedule: prod pg_cron job 'kairos-macro-sentinel' is 30 12 * * 1 — Mondays 08:30 ET, weekly. 'Runs with the daily pipeline' would lead a reader to expect a fresh regime every morning when it is up to six days old by Friday, which matters because the research scorer fails macro closed at >10 days staleness — a single missed Monday puts the US macro dimension within days of dropping out of scoring entirely. (2) Model: the route imports no callLLM and no getConfiguredModel; it is fully deterministic. The 'uses deepseek-chat' claim traces to an agent_config seed row from migration 031 that nothing reads — a dead config row that the diagram elevated into an architectural claim.

history.label: Regime is written to macro_regime — macro_signals has no regime column
history.reason: The node said 'persists the regime + summary to macro_signals'. macro_signals has no regime and no danger_score column; it holds only per-indicator rows (indicator, value, signal, description) upserted on (week_of, indicator). Regime, danger_score, summary, and raw_indicators go to macro_regime, upserted on week_of. Verified against prod information_schema, not against docs. A reader following this diagram to debug a regime would have queried the wrong table and found no such column. Also recorded that NEITHER table carries a market column — the schema fact that forces India macro to be unavailable.

history.label: <3-indicator guard → regime 'unknown', and the null it cannot store
history.reason: Shipped since 2026-07-04 and absent from the diagram, despite being the reason this agent is trustworthy on a bad-data day. Below 3 indicators the compute returns danger_score=null, regime='unknown' and publishes no verdict. The failure it replaced is visible in prod: the 2026-06-30 row reads regime='green', danger_score=0 on ZERO real indicators — a confident all-clear manufactured from nothing, which is precisely the assert-what-the-data-cannot-support defect class. Documented one honest caveat found only by reading the insert: the null NEVER reaches the table (danger_score is NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 and the write coerces null→0), so the prod 2026-07-06 row reads regime='unknown', danger_score=0. Downstream safety therefore rests entirely on consumers gating the regime STRING, which they do — a reader who assumed the null was the signal would build a broken check.

history.label: Regime enum is green/yellow/orange/red — risk-on/neutral/risk-off is a different module
history.reason: The node and the mermaid both said the output is 'risk-on / neutral / risk-off'. The route emits a four-colour enum with bands green <20, yellow 20-39, orange 40-59, red ≥60, plus an escalation override where two weight-3 indicators reading red/orange promote yellow→orange. The three-state vocabulary is real but belongs to the allocator, which NORMALIZES these colours down to three — so the diagram was showing a downstream consumer's representation as if it were this agent's output. Prod confirms the real enum: the latest row is regime='orange', danger_score=40, 6 signals triggered. Note the previously-documented bands (green<25/red≥75) were also wrong; the real cutoffs are 20/40/60.

history.label: macro_score is a genome dimension — the FEED arrow hid the money path
history.reason: The old FEED node described a generic 'advisory input to Research, Learner, Deep-Dive & Briefing', which flattened one real consumer and several stale ones into a single vague arrow. The real, consequential path: danger_score is inverted to macro_score = 100 − danger_score and consumed as one of five WEIGHTED scoring dimensions → analyst_score → direction gate → paper buys. That is a path to money and now has its own node. The Learner and Deep-Dive paths named in the old node survive only in dead edge functions. Split DISPLAY out for the genuine read-only surfaces (Markets gauge, Dashboard banner, Intelligence), and recorded the allocator as a live-but-flagged-off consumer the diagram never mentioned. USONLY added because it is the schema fact that forces India renormalization.

history.label: Verified accurate — advisory-only holds, but qualified against 'inert'
history.reason: Checked rather than assumed, and it survives: nothing in this agent auto-throttles agents, changes risk limits, or halts trading; the allocator's regime tilt is the only policy-adjacent consumer and it is gated behind an allocation_enabled flag that is OFF. The locked decision stands and the node is materially unchanged. Qualified only to prevent a misreading that the rest of this audit makes possible: with macro_score now a weighted genome dimension, 'advisory' means 'does not move the safety controls', NOT 'has no influence on what gets bought'. No churn invented — the claim was right.
